title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
shortDescription: The transfer case control module has requested the MIL be illuminated due to an internal fault.
fullDescription:
Code P0800 indicates the Transfer Case Control Module (TCCM) has detected a fault and requested the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) illuminate the Malfunction Indicator Lamp. This is typically found on 4WD or AWD vehicles with electronically controlled transfer cases.

A companion code in the transfer case module usually identifies the specific fault. The vehicle may remain in a default drive mode (typically 2WD or AWD) until the underlying issue is resolved.

Diagnosis requires scanning the TCCM directly because P0800 only reports that another module has flagged a problem — it does not identify the root cause itself.
safetyImpact: Loss of 4WD or AWD capability may reduce traction on slippery surfaces.

causes.cause: Fault in transfer case control module
Wiring or connector issues at TCCM
Low or contaminated transfer case fluid

fixSteps.title: Scan all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use a bi-directional scanner to retrieve codes from the TCCM, not just PCM.

fixSteps.title: Address TCCM codes
fixSteps.instruction: Repair the specific fault reported by the transfer case module.

faq.a: Usually yes in 2WD, but 4WD may be disabled.
No, it is specific to the transfer case on 4WD/AWD vehicles.

title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit
shortDescription: A fault has been detected in the circuit that prevents reverse gear engagement at high speeds.
fullDescription:
P0801 indicates the PCM has detected an electrical fault in the reverse inhibit control circuit. This safety feature prevents drivers from shifting into reverse while traveling forward at speed, which would cause catastrophic transmission damage.

On manual transmissions this is often a solenoid that locks the reverse gate; on automatics it may be a valve body solenoid or shift lock mechanism.

Until the circuit is repaired reverse engagement may be intermittent or fail entirely.
safetyImpact: Reverse may not engage or may engage when it should not, risking drivetrain damage.

causes.cause: Faulty PCM or TCM output driver

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Measure solenoid resistance and compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check harness for damage between PCM and solenoid.

faq.a: It can allow reverse at speed, so repair promptly.

title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
shortDescription: The TCM is requesting the MIL but the circuit is open.
fullDescription:
P0802 indicates the Transmission Control Module has requested MIL illumination via an open circuit. This means either the TCM has logged a fault or the communication line between TCM and PCM is broken.

Scanning the TCM directly is essential — the reported issue often lies elsewhere in the transmission system.

fixSteps.title: Check communication
fixSteps.instruction: Verify CAN bus integrity between TCM and PCM.

fixSteps.title: Repair open circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Fix wiring or replace module as needed.

faq.a: Only if wiring checks pass and the module is confirmed faulty.

title: 1-4 Upshift (Skip Shift) Solenoid Control Circuit
shortDescription: A fault exists in the skip-shift solenoid circuit used on some manual transmissions.
fullDescription:
P0803 sets when the PCM detects an electrical fault in the skip-shift (1-4) solenoid circuit. This feature, found on some performance manual transmissions, forces a 1-4 upshift at light throttle to improve fuel economy.

A failure typically means the skip-shift feature stops working or stays engaged. While not safety-critical, it will illuminate the MIL and may fail emissions testing.
safetyImpact: Minimal — affects fuel economy feature only.

fixSteps.title: Inspect solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Locate solenoid on transmission and check connector.

faq.a: Most enthusiasts disable it; it only affects fuel economy.

title: 1-4 Upshift (Skip Shift) Lamp Control Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in the skip-shift indicator lamp circuit.
fullDescription:
P0804 indicates a malfunction in the control circuit for the skip-shift indicator lamp on the instrument cluster. The lamp tells the driver when skip-shift is forcing a 1-4 upshift.

The root cause is usually a bulb, wiring, or instrument cluster issue, not the transmission itself.

fixSteps.title: Test wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity between PCM and cluster.

faq.a: No, only the indicator lamp is affected.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: The PCM has detected a general fault in the clutch position sensor circuit.
fullDescription:
P0805 is set when the clutch position sensor signal is outside expected parameters. The sensor tells the PCM whether the clutch pedal is depressed, which affects start enable, cruise control cancel, and shift timing.

A failure can prevent the engine from cranking or cause other driveability issues.
safetyImpact: Engine may not start; cruise control may behave oddly.
symptoms: No start unless clutch specific position

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor signal
fixSteps.instruction: Watch live data as pedal is pressed.

fixSteps.title: Adjust or replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Correct adjustment or replace if faulty.

faq.a: It depends on whether the signal is stuck at pressed or released.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: The clutch position sensor signal is out of the expected range.
fullDescription:
P0806 is set when the clutch pedal position sensor reports a value that does not make sense given vehicle operation — for example, not returning to a zero position or exceeding maximum travel.

Causes are usually mechanical: a bent bracket, broken pedal return spring, or a failing sensor.
safetyImpact: Shift quality or start enable may be affected.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor range
fixSteps.instruction: Graph sensor data across full pedal travel.

faq.a: No, it is the sensor that monitors pedal position.

title: Clutch Position Control Error
shortDescription: The clutch actuator did not reach its commanded position.
fullDescription:
P0810 is primarily seen on vehicles with automated manual transmissions or dual-clutch systems. It indicates the clutch actuator failed to achieve the position commanded by the TCM.

Causes range from low hydraulic pressure to a worn clutch pack to an actuator motor failure. This code often accompanies poor engagement or jerky launches.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may lose drive temporarily or launch roughly.

fixSteps.title: Perform clutch adaptation
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory tool to relearn clutch.

faq.q: Can the clutch be adapted without replacement?
faq.a: Sometimes — try adaptation first.

title: Excessive Clutch Slippage
shortDescription: The PCM/TCM has detected excessive clutch slip.
fullDescription:
P0811 is stored when the transmission detects the clutch is slipping more than allowed. The control module compares engine RPM to output RPM; when the ratio indicates slip beyond a threshold, this code sets.

In manual/automated vehicles this usually means a worn clutch disc; in some automatics it points to a torque converter lock-up clutch issue.
safetyImpact: Power delivery may be compromised; continued driving can destroy the clutch.

fixSteps.title: Confirm slip
fixSteps.instruction: Perform road test while monitoring RPM vs speed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for oil contamination
fixSteps.instruction: Check rear main seal and input seals.

fixSteps.title: Replace clutch
fixSteps.instruction: Install new clutch kit and resurface flywheel.

faq.a: Minimally — excessive slip will destroy the clutch and possibly flywheel.

title: Reverse Input Circuit
shortDescription: The PCM has detected a fault in the reverse input circuit.
fullDescription:
P0812 indicates an issue with the signal that tells the PCM when the transmission is in reverse. This input is used to enable reverse lamps, disable cruise control, and adjust shift strategy.

Common causes include a failed reverse switch, wiring, or range sensor.
safetyImpact: Reverse lights may not work; backup camera may not activate.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Use DMM to check switch continuity in reverse.

faq.a: They are a safety feature required to be working.

title: Upshift Switch Circuit
shortDescription: Fault detected in the upshift request switch circuit.
fullDescription: P0815 sets when the driver-requested upshift switch (used on vehicles with manumatic or paddle shifters) has an electrical issue. The switch may be stuck, the wiring shorted, or the steering wheel clockspring damaged.
safetyImpact: Manual shifting mode may not work.

fixSteps.title: Inspect clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: Check clockspring continuity if paddles are on wheel.

faq.a: Usually yes — only manual upshift requests are affected.

title: Downshift Switch Circuit
shortDescription: Fault detected in the downshift request switch circuit.
fullDescription: P0816 indicates an electrical problem in the driver downshift request switch. Symptoms and causes mirror P0815 but affect the downshift paddle or lever.
safetyImpact: Manual downshift requests may not work.

faq.a: Yes, automatic mode is unaffected.

title: Starter Disable Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in the starter disable safety circuit.
fullDescription:
P0817 sets when the PCM detects a fault in the circuit that prevents the starter from cranking unless the clutch is depressed or the transmission is in Park/Neutral.

This is a safety feature — a fault may allow cranking in gear or prevent cranking in Park.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may crank in gear causing sudden movement.

fixSteps.title: Test safety switch
fixSteps.instruction: Check switch continuity at correct position.

faq.a: Yes — fix promptly to prevent cranking in gear.

title: Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit
shortDescription: A fault exists in the driveline disconnect switch circuit.
fullDescription: P0818 indicates the PCM has seen an abnormal signal from the driveline disconnect switch, used on some clutch-pedal-equipped vehicles to interrupt drive. Causes are similar to other clutch input circuits.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fix wiring or install new switch.

faq.a: Functionally similar; specifics vary by manufacturer.

title: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in the gear lever X-Y position sensor.
fullDescription: P0820 sets on manual transmissions that use an X-Y sensor at the shifter to detect which gear the driver has selected. A fault here means the PCM cannot determine selected gear, which affects shift timing and engine rev-matching on some vehicles.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate at base of shifter and test.

faq.a: Some are; consult service data.

title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit
shortDescription: Circuit fault in clutch pedal switch A.
fullDescription:
P0830 sets when the PCM detects an electrical problem in the clutch pedal switch A circuit. The switch is used for engine start enable and cruise control cancellation.

Failure may prevent cranking or cause cruise to drop out unexpectedly.
safetyImpact: Engine may not start; cruise control issues.

faq.a: Some vehicles use two — A for start, B for cruise.

title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit Open
shortDescription: The clutch pedal switch B circuit is open.
fullDescription: P0833 indicates the secondary clutch pedal switch circuit is open — no signal is reaching the PCM. Causes are typically wiring or switch failure, occasionally a pedal misadjustment.

faq.a: No, different switch on same pedal.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
shortDescription: Circuit fault in transmission fluid pressure sensor A.
fullDescription:
P0840 is set when the PCM detects an electrical fault in the transmission fluid pressure sensor A circuit. This sensor is critical for monitoring line pressure and adjusting shift timing.

Causes include sensor failure, harness damage, or occasionally low fluid level causing erratic readings.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor live data and test with DMM.

faq.a: Often yes — pan must be dropped.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Range/Performance
shortDescription: Transmission fluid pressure sensor A reading is implausible.
fullDescription:
P0841 indicates pressure sensor A is reporting values that don't match operating conditions. A pressure reading that doesn't change with line pressure, or varies erratically, sets this code.

Internal transmission hydraulic faults are common causes in addition to sensor issues.
safetyImpact: Shift behavior may be severely affected.

fixSteps.title: Internal repair
fixSteps.instruction: Service valve body or replace sensor.

faq.a: Sometimes, if fluid is old or contaminated.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low
shortDescription: Transmission fluid pressure sensor A signal is too low.
fullDescription: P0842 indicates pressure sensor A voltage is below the minimum threshold. This is usually caused by a shorted sensor or ground wire, but true low hydraulic pressure can cause it too.
safetyImpact: Transmission may slip or enter limp mode.

faq.a: Only briefly — damage risk is high.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
shortDescription: Transmission fluid pressure sensor A signal is too high.
fullDescription: P0843 sets when pressure sensor A voltage is above the maximum threshold, indicating an open circuit, short to voltage, or extreme high pressure condition.
safetyImpact: Shift quality and gear selection may suffer.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for open or shorts to power.

faq.a: Open circuits and connector corrosion are common.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent signal from pressure sensor A.
fullDescription: P0844 indicates the signal from transmission pressure sensor A drops out or spikes intermittently. Loose connectors and chafed wiring are prime suspects.

faq.q: Why is it hard to find?
faq.a: Intermittent faults often require wiggle testing under load.

title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in the park/neutral safety switch input.
fullDescription:
P0850 indicates the PCM sees an abnormal signal from the park/neutral safety switch. This switch enables cranking only in Park or Neutral and informs engine and transmission strategies about gear state.

A fault may prevent cranking or allow cranking in gear.

faq.a: Related but specifically the PNP portion.

title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit Low
shortDescription: Park/neutral switch input is low.
fullDescription: P0851 sets when the PNP input voltage is below the expected range. Common causes are short to ground or a failed switch stuck closed.

faq.a: Yes — diagnose promptly.

title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit High
shortDescription: Park/neutral switch input is high.
fullDescription: P0852 sets when the PNP input voltage exceeds the expected range, indicating open circuit or short to voltage. The vehicle may not allow starting in Park.

fixSteps.title: Test circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Check for open or short to power.

faq.a: High circuit may block starter enable.

title: Drive Switch Input Circuit
shortDescription: Fault detected in the drive switch input.
fullDescription: P0853 indicates an abnormal signal from the drive switch input. On vehicles with separate drive position input this switch tells the PCM when drive is selected for shift scheduling.

faq.a: Related but focuses on drive position only.

title: Traction Control Input Signal
shortDescription: Fault in traction control input to PCM.
fullDescription: P0856 sets when the traction control module input to the PCM is invalid. This input is used by the PCM to reduce torque during wheel slip. A fault may disable traction control cooperation between modules.

faq.a: Yes, but with reduced traction assistance.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Range/Performance
shortDescription: Pressure sensor C reports implausible values.
fullDescription: P0871 sets when transmission pressure sensor C shows readings that do not correspond with operating conditions. Internal transmission issues or a failing sensor are typical causes.

faq.a: Yes, transmissions may have A, B, C, D sensors.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Low
shortDescription: Pressure sensor C circuit voltage is low.
fullDescription: P0872 indicates pressure sensor C voltage is below threshold. Usually caused by a short to ground, connector corrosion, or a failed sensor.

faq.a: A third pressure sensor in complex transmissions.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit High
shortDescription: Pressure sensor C circuit voltage is high.
fullDescription: P0873 indicates sensor C voltage is above threshold due to open circuit, short to voltage, or failed sensor. Diagnosis mirrors other high-circuit pressure sensor codes.

faq.q: Should I replace the whole valve body?
faq.a: Only if sensor replacement doesn't resolve.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit
shortDescription: Circuit fault in pressure sensor D.
fullDescription: P0875 sets when the PCM sees an electrical issue in pressure sensor D. Sensors A-D correspond to different hydraulic circuits within the transmission.

faq.a: Yes, on complex automatics.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Range/Performance
shortDescription: Pressure sensor D reading is implausible.
fullDescription: P0876 sets when sensor D reports values inconsistent with operating conditions, often due to internal transmission issues or sensor drift.

faq.a: Yes — sustained issues can damage the transmission.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
shortDescription: Pressure sensor D voltage is low.
fullDescription: P0877 indicates pressure sensor D circuit voltage is below threshold, typically from a short to ground or failed sensor.

faq.a: No — clears once fault is fixed and reset.

title: TCM Power Input Signal
shortDescription: Fault in Transmission Control Module power input signal.
fullDescription:
P0880 indicates the TCM power input signal is abnormal. This may be caused by a bad fuse, corroded connector, or a weak battery feed to the TCM.

The TCM requires stable power for proper shift control; low or interrupted power can cause erratic shifting and default strategies.

fixSteps.title: Verify voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm TCM power supply is stable.

faq.a: A weak battery or bad ground can, yes.

title: TCM Power Input Signal Low
shortDescription: TCM power input signal is low.
fullDescription: P0882 indicates the power feed to the TCM is below minimum threshold. Usually caused by corroded grounds, loose battery terminals, or a damaged fuse holder.

faq.a: Yes — always verify charging first.

title: TCM Power Input Signal High
shortDescription: TCM power input signal is high.
fullDescription: P0883 sets when the TCM power input exceeds normal voltage. This may indicate a failing voltage regulator or a charging system overvoltage condition.
safetyImpact: Possible TCM damage if overvoltage persists.

faq.a: Yes — fix promptly.

title: TCM Power Input Signal Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent TCM power input.
fullDescription: P0884 sets when the TCM power signal drops out intermittently. Causes are usually loose connections or a worn ignition switch.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor TCM voltage while wiggling harness.

faq.a: Yes, especially on older vehicles.

title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in TCM power relay sense circuit.
fullDescription: P0890 indicates the PCM/TCM cannot confirm the TCM power relay state via the sense line. The relay itself may be fine but the feedback signal is missing or incorrect.

faq.a: Usually in underhood fuse box.

title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: TCM relay sense signal is implausible.
fullDescription: P0891 sets when the TCM power relay sense line shows values that do not match the commanded relay state. Typical causes include a failing relay contact or corrupted wiring.

faq.q: Can I swap with another relay?
faq.a: Often yes — identical relays in the fuse box.

title: Transmission Component Slipping
shortDescription: The TCM has detected slippage in a transmission component.
fullDescription:
P0894 is set when the TCM sees a clutch pack, band, or torque converter slipping more than tolerated. Unlike P0730 family, this is a generic component-slip indicator.

Slippage is often caused by worn friction material, low pressure, or stuck valve body passages.

fixSteps.title: Pressure test
fixSteps.instruction: Use external gauge on line pressure.

faq.a: Worth trying on early slip with burnt fluid.

title: Shift Time Too Short
shortDescription: Shifts are completing faster than expected.
fullDescription: P0895 indicates the time the transmission takes to complete a shift is below the expected window. This usually means harsh, abrupt shifts caused by excessive line pressure or stuck accumulator/valve body components.
safetyImpact: Harsh shifting is uncomfortable and stresses drivetrain.

faq.a: Yes — it wears components faster.

title: Shift Time Too Long
shortDescription: Shifts are taking longer than expected.
fullDescription: P0896 sets when transmission shifts exceed their expected duration. This is often due to low fluid pressure, worn clutches, or restricted hydraulic passages causing lingering overlap.
safetyImpact: Slipping can quickly destroy the transmission.

fixSteps.title: Internal repair
fixSteps.instruction: Rebuild if friction material is worn.

faq.a: Yes on early stages.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit/Open
shortDescription: Clutch actuator circuit is open.
fullDescription: P0900 indicates the clutch actuator control circuit is open — typical on automated manual and DCT vehicles. Causes include broken wires, failed actuator motor, or connector issues.
safetyImpact: Clutch may not engage, causing loss of drive.

faq.a: Mostly — also automated manuals.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Clutch actuator circuit performance is out of range.
fullDescription: P0901 indicates the clutch actuator is not responding as commanded. The position feedback may not match the command signal.

fixSteps.title: Adaptation
fixSteps.instruction: Run clutch adaptation with factory tool.

faq.a: Yes, especially after fluid service.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Low
shortDescription: Clutch actuator circuit voltage low.
fullDescription: P0902 indicates the clutch actuator control circuit voltage is below threshold, usually caused by a short to ground or a shorted actuator coil.

faq.a: Low = short, open = broken wire.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit High
shortDescription: Clutch actuator circuit voltage high.
fullDescription: P0903 indicates the clutch actuator control circuit voltage is above threshold due to an open or short to voltage.

fixSteps.title: Test harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for opens and shorts to B+.

faq.a: All three prevent clutch operation.

title: Gate Select Position Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in gate select position sensor circuit.
fullDescription: P0904 is set when the gate select position sensor circuit (used in automated transmissions to select shift gates) reports an electrical fault.

faq.a: Gate is lateral, shift is longitudinal.

title: Gate Select Position Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Gate select sensor reading out of range.
fullDescription: P0905 indicates gate select position sensor values are inconsistent with expected movement. Mechanical binding or sensor drift are common causes.

faq.a: Yes — factory-level tool usually needed.

title: Gate Select Position Circuit Low
shortDescription: Gate select sensor signal low.
fullDescription: P0906 indicates the gate select position sensor voltage is below threshold. Usually caused by a short to ground or failed sensor.

faq.a: Yes, especially on older systems.

title: Gate Select Position Circuit High
shortDescription: Gate select sensor signal high.
fullDescription: P0907 indicates gate select position sensor voltage is above threshold, from open or short to voltage.

fixSteps.title: Test harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for open or short to B+.

faq.a: Disconnect sensor and measure harness.

title: Gate Select Control Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in gate select actuator control.
fullDescription: P0908 indicates an electrical problem in the gate select actuator output circuit. The TCM commands the actuator to move the shift fork laterally between gates.

faq.a: Sometimes — more often replaced as an assembly.

title: Gate Select Control Performance
shortDescription: Gate select actuator performance fault.
fullDescription: P0909 sets when the gate select actuator does not perform the commanded movement correctly, often due to wear, binding, or adaptation drift.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Install new actuator if relearn fails.

faq.a: Varies — many last the life of the vehicle.

title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit Low
shortDescription: Gate select actuator circuit voltage low.
fullDescription: P0910 indicates the gate select actuator circuit voltage is below threshold — typically a short to ground or failed motor.

faq.a: Often no — call a tow.

title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit High
shortDescription: Gate select actuator circuit voltage high.
fullDescription: P0911 indicates the gate select actuator circuit voltage is above threshold — an open or short to voltage.

fixSteps.title: Test harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for open or short to power.

faq.a: Usually OEM-only, can be expensive.

title: Gate Select Actuator Intermittent
shortDescription: Gate select actuator signal intermittent.
fullDescription: P0912 sets when the gate select actuator signal drops out intermittently, usually from a loose connector or fatigued wire.

faq.a: Often — try road-test wiggle.

title: Gear Shift Position Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in gear shift position circuit.
fullDescription: P0913 sets when the PCM/TCM sees an electrical fault on the gear shift position (longitudinal) sensor circuit. Used on automated manual and DCT systems.

faq.a: No — this is shift axis (engagement depth).

title: Gear Shift Position Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Gear shift position sensor reading out of range.
fullDescription: P0914 indicates the shift position sensor reports values that do not match commanded positions. Sensor drift or binding is common.

faq.a: Yes — actuator issues can cause false sensor codes.

title: Gear Shift Position Circuit Low
shortDescription: Gear shift position sensor circuit low.
fullDescription: P0915 indicates low voltage on the shift position sensor circuit — short to ground or failed sensor are typical.

faq.a: Inspect connector for corrosion.

title: Gear Shift Position Circuit High
shortDescription: Gear shift position sensor circuit high.
fullDescription: P0916 indicates high voltage on the shift position sensor circuit — open or short to voltage.

faq.a: Connector corrosion is very common.

title: Gear Shift Position Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent shift position signal.
fullDescription: P0917 sets when the shift position signal is intermittent. Usually a connector, terminal fit, or wiring harness issue.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Fix terminal fit or replace harness.

faq.a: It can help but a proper repair is better.

title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in forward shift actuator control.
fullDescription: P0918 sets when the forward shift actuator control circuit has an electrical fault. The actuator drives the shift rail forward to engage specific gears.

faq.a: Partially — full test usually needs removal.

title: Gear Shift Position Control Error
shortDescription: Shift position control did not reach target.
fullDescription: P0919 indicates the TCM commanded a shift position and the actuator did not achieve it within the time window. Common causes are worn actuators, synchros, or internal hydraulic problems.

faq.a: Sometimes fluid service addresses early issues.

title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Low
shortDescription: Forward shift actuator circuit voltage low.
fullDescription: P0920 indicates the forward shift actuator control circuit voltage is below threshold, typically a short to ground.

faq.a: Yes — there are separate codes for rearward actuator.

title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Shift lock solenoid performance issue.
fullDescription: P0928 sets when the gear shift lock solenoid (which prevents shifter movement out of Park without brake depressed) operates outside expected parameters. Usually an internal solenoid issue.
safetyImpact: May prevent shifting out of Park or allow it without brake.

faq.a: Most vehicles have a shift lock override slot.

title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid Control Circuit High
shortDescription: Shift lock solenoid circuit voltage high.
fullDescription: P0929 indicates the shift lock solenoid circuit voltage is above threshold — open or short to voltage.

faq.a: Yes — can be tied to key removal logic.
